questions.text: Quick Revision - Asexual and Sexual Reproduction

definitionBean.title: Asexual and Sexual Reproduction
definitionBean.definition: The process by which living organisms produce new individuals similar to themselves is called 'Reproduction'. Reproduction occurring through a single parent is 'asexual', and through the fusion of male and female gametes is 'sexual'[cite: 16].
definitionBean.explanation: In asexual reproduction, variations during DNA replication are low (e.g., fission, budding, regeneration), whereas in sexual reproduction, involvement of two parents generates higher genetic variations helpful for evolution[cite: 16].
importantPoints: Asexual reproduction: Single organism takes part, offspring is a clone[cite: 16]
Sexual reproduction: Fusion of male and female gametes (Fertilization) takes place[cite: 16]
Fission (Amoeba) and Budding (Hydra/Yeast) are asexual methods[cite: 16]
Sexual reproduction is found in flowering plants and higher animals[cite: 16]

questions.text: Quick Revision - Reproduction in Flower and Human Reproductive System

definitionBean.title: Reproduction in Flower and Human Reproductive System
definitionBean.definition: A flower is the reproductive organ of plants containing stamen (male) and carpel (female); and in humans, reproduction is carried out via the male reproductive system (testes) and female reproductive system (ovaries)[cite: 16].
definitionBean.explanation: After pollination, pollen grains reach the stigma and form a zygote through fertilization[cite: 16]. In humans, fertilization takes place in the fallopian tube[cite: 16].
importantPoints: Stamen: Production of pollen grains (male gamete)[cite: 16]
Human Testes: Sperm production and testosterone hormone[cite: 16]
Human Ovaries: Ovum production and estrogen hormone[cite: 16]

parts.statement: Write differences between asexual and sexual reproduction. Why is reproduction necessary for organisms[cite: 16]?
parts.correct_answer: Asexual involves one parent, sexual involves two parents[cite: 16].
parts.explanation: In asexual reproduction, only a single parent takes part and gametes are not formed, whereas in sexual reproduction, two parents (male and female) take part and fusion of gametes occurs[cite: 16]. Reproduction is necessary to maintain the existence and continuity of species of organisms[cite: 16].

parts.statement: Explain fission and regeneration with examples[cite: 16].
parts.explanation: In fission, a single organism divides into two or more parts (e.g., Amoeba)[cite: 16]. In regeneration, if an organism is cut due to any reason, its cut pieces develop into new organisms (e.g., Planaria or Hydra)[cite: 16].

parts.statement: Draw a labeled diagram of an ideal flower and describe its main reproductive organs[cite: 16].
parts.correct_answer: Stamen and carpel are main reproductive organs of a flower[cite: 16].
parts.explanation: The main reproductive organs of a flower are the stamen (male organ, containing anther) and carpel (female organ, containing stigma, style, and ovary)[cite: 16].

parts.statement: Clarify the difference between self-pollination and cross-pollination[cite: 16].
parts.correct_answer: Self-pollination occurs within same flower/plant, cross-pollination between different plants[cite: 16].
parts.explanation: When pollen grains of a flower reach the stigma of the same flower or another flower of the same plant, self-pollination occurs; when pollen grains of a flower go to the stigma of a flower of another plant, it is called cross-pollination[cite: 16].

parts.statement: Name the main organs of the human male reproductive system and state the functions of the testes[cite: 16].
parts.correct_answer: Testes, vas deferens, penis; testes produce sperm[cite: 16].
parts.explanation: Main organs of the human male reproductive system: Testes, vas deferens, and penis[cite: 16]. The primary function of the testes is to produce male gametes (sperm) and secrete the testosterone hormone[cite: 16].

parts.statement: Where does the process of fertilization take place in the human female reproductive system[cite: 16]?
parts.explanation: In human females, fertilization (fusion of sperm and ovum) takes place in the fallopian tube (oviduct), after which the zygote gets implanted in the uterus[cite: 16].
